judge: LLM-as-a-judge: Claude (claude-opus-5-5), 2026-11-19, from model knowledge of TNAU Crop Production Guide practice; NOT a human expert

1: Names no variety; TNAU samba options for Thanjavur (e.g. CR 1009, CR 1009 Sub1, ADT 46, CO 50) not given, only 'consult officer'
2: Matches TNAU groundnut seasons: Adipattam Jun-Jul (rainfed), Karthigai Oct-Nov, irrigated Dec-Jan/Jan-Feb
3: 100-110 kg urea/acre fits ~120 kg N/ha (short duration) but TNAU splits N in 4 equal doses incl. heading; no duration or LCC/soil-test adjustment
4: Lists leaf curl virus (whitefly-borne), the classic cause of curling+yellowing, but leads with nitrogen deficiency and gives no virus management (rogueing, whitefly control)
5: Doses match TNAU FAW advice: emamectin benzoate 5 SG ~80 g/acre, chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC ~80 ml/acre, azadirachtin 1500 ppm 5 ml/L, whorl application
6: Gives no forecast or irrigation advice although Madurai is named; only asks for the crop
7: No answer: only asks for the district (follow-up only, no crop suggested)
8: 9-12 months is low for TN varieties: Poovan/Robusta ~11-14 months, Red banana 15-18 months; no variety distinction
9: 75-90 cm rows is the normal ridge spacing (TNAU ~80 cm) but omits TNAU wide-row/SSI 150 cm (5 ft) spacing
12: Yes; black cotton soil suits cotton and Virudhunagar is a rainfed cotton district; advice on drainage is sound
13: 50-75 L every 4-7 days is far below TNAU guidance (drip ~65 L per palm per DAY in summer)
14: 7-9 months after planting, when leaves yellow and dry, matches TNAU
15: Standard recipe uses 2 kg jaggery and 2 kg pulse flour per 200 L with ~48 h fermentation; answer halves both and says 2-7 days
16: Neem 5 ml/L and imidacloprid/thiamethoxam at label-range doses are accepted whitefly options; misses yellow sticky traps
18: FYM/compost, green manures (sunnhemp, daincha), residue incorporation, vermicompost, legumes, mulching: standard practice
19: Gives 50:50:30 kg NPK per ACRE plus top dressings; TNAU varietal brinjal is ~50:50:30 basal per HECTARE (+50 kg N top), so doses are ~2.5x too high
22: Drainage through bunds/channels, inspecting for lodging and post-rain pest/disease checks is appropriate
48: TNAU black gram seed rate 20 kg/ha = 8 kg/acre; answer 8-10 (6-8 line sown) matches
49: Dry to ~12-14% moisture, clean, dunnage off floor/walls, neem leaves, fumigation only on officer advice: matches standard practice
10: Salt-water flotation to remove light seed, wash, then carbendazim/bio-agent seed treatment: matches TNAU seed treatment practice
11: Correct pathogen (Pyricularia/Magnaporthe oryzae), weather and excess-N risk factors, resistant varieties and fungicide control
17: No answer: asks for the district although Ramanathapuram is in the question
20: Yes; drip saves water and improves bulb uniformity and yield in onion, as TNAU recommends
21: Older-leaf yellowing first, pale plant, stunting, thin stems: correct nitrogen-deficiency symptoms
23: Sanitation, bund burrow destruction, traps, 2% zinc phosphide bait (25 g in 975 g = 2.5%, close) and anticoagulant baits: standard rodent control
25: Dry to 12-14% moisture, clean, cool, dunnage, clean bags away from walls, neem leaves: standard practice
26: No answer: only asks for the district; no intercrop (e.g. banana, cocoa, pepper, pulses) suggested
27: Split application timing is right, but 200-300 g MoP/plant/year is low; TNAU ~330 g K2O/plant (~550 g MoP) in splits
28: Pendimethalin pre-emergence ~1 L/acre is right; imazethapyr 75-100 ml/acre is well below the TNAU rate (~0.1 kg a.i./ha = ~400 ml/acre of 10 SL)
29: Gives no yield figure (TNAU rainfed ragi ~1-1.5 t/ha, roughly 400-600 kg/acre); only 'consult officer'
30: Irrigation, boron/zinc sprays and hopper/powdery mildew control are relevant but omits the standard NAA 20 ppm spray
31: CR 1009 (Savithri) is right for samba, but durations are wrong: ADT 39 and CO 51 are short-duration (~105-125 d), not 155-160 / 130-135 d
32: Jun-Jul, Oct-Nov and irrigated Jan-Feb groundnut seasons match TNAU (season names loosely used)
33: 45-50 kg urea/acre is about half the TNAU recommendation (~100-130 kg/acre) and contradicts the English answer to the same question (Q3)
34: Identifies whitefly-borne tomato leaf curl virus as a main cause, with sucking pests and nutrient/water causes, and advises checking for whiteflies
36: Says it has no rain information although the system has a district weather service
39: Carbendazim 2 g/kg is right, but Pseudomonas (TNAU 10 g/kg) and Trichoderma (4 g/kg) rates are swapped and 200 g Azospirillum per kg seed is far too high
40: Correct symptoms and N/water management; tricyclazole 75 WP 125 g/acre is below the TNAU ~200 g/acre (500 g/ha)
44: Pearl millet, sorghum, ragi, kodo and barnyard millet suit dry Ramanathapuram

note: Q1-Q9,Q12-Q16,Q18,Q19,Q22,Q48,Q49 answered in the first run; the other answered rows in the retry runs. All 40 answers from gemini-2.5-flash. 10 rows not answered (Gemini free-tier quota).
